---
title: "017 — Secure public launch"
---

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Launch Mayon on the public internet gated so only the owner — and
explicitly invited people — can reach the app and its APIs. The work began as
idea 002-secure-public-launch, whose decisions.md verdict picked the
password-plus-MFA gate built into the app (the owner's own card, chosen because
learning is a first-class goal in a hobby project), with a reverse-proxy
basic-auth floor as the one-evening on-ramp while the gate was built; the
zero-trust edge stayed the standing fallback, and multi-user isolation died at
the card table on the owner's ruling.

**Why.** The prod stack had no front door at all, and the winning card's
playthrough had named the characteristic failure mode precisely: the gate fails
one unguarded route at a time, silently. That shaped the whole design —
enforcement had to be centralized at the server seam, never left to per-route
discipline. Owner rulings bounded the rest: security is opt-in (first-run setup
is skippable, with no re-nagging); MFA is mandatory whenever the gate is locked
(no password-only mode); sessions last until the end of the calendar day; the
hostile-takeover risk of a stranger enabling security first on a public URL is
explicitly accepted, with server-side CLI recovery as the way back; and there is
no registration, no self-service reset, no per-user data isolation — identities
exist for access control only.

**Outcome & reversals.** Merged as PR #19 (2026-09-03) and shipped in 0.6.0,
all seven user stories intact. One Fastify `onRequest` hook registered before
every route plugin covers all current and future capabilities; a CI sweep test
enumerates every registered route and asserts uniform 401 without a session —
the unguarded-endpoint failure mode converted into a permanent invariant.
Passwords hash with argon2id; TOTP verifies with a replay guard and ±1-step
drift tolerance; TOTP secrets are AES-256-GCM-wrapped under a key held outside
Postgres, so a stolen `pg_dump` yields no usable credentials; sessions are
opaque tokens stored hash-only, expiring at local midnight; login attempts run
a per-IP exponential-delay ladder; invites hand over one-time passwords with
immediate revocation killing live sessions; the Caddy floor ships as release
templates, using compose's `!override` tag to un-publish the app port so the
single-entrance property is checkable. Adversarial review blockers were fixed
pre-merge, and fast-follows repaired real findings: a TOTP input pattern that
rejected every valid code, and same-origin 403s behind host-rewriting proxies
(plus trustProxy hardening and nginx forwarding headers). The full wire
contract is preserved at
[appendices/017-auth-api.md](appendices/017-auth-api.md).

**Learnings.**

- A gate enforced once at the seam turns "every endpoint must remember to
  check" into a structural property — and the sweep test keeps it one.
- Optional security is still a decision surface: the open state must be visible
  and honest, or "optional" silently reads as "broken".
- A stolen database yielding nothing usable is a storage-layer property: hash
  passwords, wrap MFA secrets under a key outside the database, store only
  token hashes.
- Un-publishing a port requires compose `!override`, because `ports:` lists
  merge on override — the floor's wall would otherwise be silently void.
- Deletion can be the security feature: with no self-service reset, the
  classic bypass door does not exist to be forgotten.
